articles.title: Zero Latency Study: VR Is the Most In-Demand Attraction at Entertainment Venues
articles.summary: A consumer study of 2,386 participants across five countries found that location-based VR ranked first among desired attractions at 93%, ahead of arcades, bowling, escape rooms, mini golf, laser tag, and go-karts. Critically, VR is the only major attraction category to see rising consumer demand since 2023. For FEC operators, the findings represent a clear opportunity to add or expand VR offerings to meet unmet guest demand.

articles.title: MirraArena Multiplayer VR Averages 1,500+ Sessions Per Month at China FEC Venues
articles.summary: Multiplayer VR platform MirraArena has reported strong performance across four FEC locations in China, averaging over 1,500 game sessions and nearly 5,000 arena entries per venue each month. The results demonstrate that well-executed multiplayer VR can drive meaningful repeat visitation and throughput. Operators evaluating VR investments will find the operating data a useful benchmark.

articles.title: Zero Latency VR Sets Release Date for Jumanji: The Lost Levels, Its First Hand-Tracked Title
articles.summary: Zero Latency VR has announced the launch date for Jumanji: The Lost Levels, marking the company's first fully hand-tracked location-based VR experience. The move to hand-tracking removes the need for controllers, potentially lowering operational complexity and improving guest accessibility. FEC operators running Zero Latency systems should prepare for the new title rollout and the marketing opportunity a major IP brings.

articles.title: Adventure Landing Closes Raleigh Location After 38 Years
articles.summary: Adventure Landing, a longstanding multi-attraction FEC brand, has abruptly shuttered its Raleigh location after 38 years of operation. The sudden closure highlights ongoing challenges facing traditional FEC formats that have not modernized their offerings. Operators should take note of the competitive pressures driving legacy venues out of key markets.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Signs Lease on First Montana Location
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment, a fast-growing trampoline and multi-attraction FEC chain, has signed a lease for its first Montana venue, continuing its national expansion strategy. The brand has also been converting former retail anchor stores — such as a vacant Dillard's in Denton, Texas — into entertainment centers. The moves signal continued appetite for FEC expansion into underserved markets and adaptive reuse of retail space.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Converts Former Dillard's into Denton FEC This Fall
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is transforming a shuttered Dillard's department store in Denton, Texas, into a full-scale family entertainment center slated to open this fall. The project is part of Launch's broader strategy of repurposing large vacant retail spaces for FEC use, a trend gaining traction across the industry. For operators and developers, the project offers a model for cost-effective venue development in high-traffic retail corridors.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Intensifies $13.3 Billion Buildout of Indoor Entertainment Centers
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia is accelerating a $13.3 billion investment program to develop indoor entertainment centers across the Kingdom as part of its Vision 2030 diversification agenda. The scale of development represents one of the largest government-backed FEC buildouts in history, creating significant opportunities for international operators, suppliers, and designers. Industry players with global ambitions should be closely watching procurement and partnership opportunities emerging from this initiative.

articles.title: Seder Group and ProFun Launch SPOC, a New Turnkey FEC Operator for Saudi Market
articles.summary: Seder Group and ProFun have announced the formation of SPOC, a joint venture designed to provide fully integrated operations management for theme parks, water parks, FECs, and other attractions in Saudi Arabia. The platform combines ProFun's international attractions expertise with Seder's local Saudi operational infrastructure and workforce. As Saudi Arabia's entertainment buildout accelerates, SPOC positions itself as a one-stop operating partner for developers entering the market.

articles.title: Social Gaming Venue Time Mission to Open Downtown Boston Location in Early 2027
articles.summary: Time Mission, a social gaming venue concept, has announced a downtown Boston location with construction beginning later this year and an opening targeted for early 2027. The format, which blends competitive social gaming with food and beverage, is part of a growing wave of experiential entertainment venues targeting urban markets. FEC operators should monitor this category as it competes for the same young adult demographic.

articles.title: Family Entertainment Group Reaches 100-Location Milestone with Margaritaville at Sea Partnership
articles.summary: Family Entertainment Group LLC has celebrated its 100th location milestone by announcing a landmark partnership with Margaritaville at Sea, extending its entertainment concepts onto cruise ships. The milestone underscores strong franchise growth in the FEC sector and highlights an emerging channel — cruise and hospitality venues — for FEC-style entertainment deployment. Operators and franchisors tracking growth benchmarks in the industry will find this a notable data point.

articles.title: Minnesota Bowling Centers Reinvent Themselves to Stay Competitive
articles.summary: A feature on Minnesota's bowling industry examines how operators are diversifying beyond traditional lanes into food and beverage, arcade games, private events, and other FEC-style attractions to drive revenue and relevance. The trend mirrors a national shift away from stand-alone bowling toward full-service entertainment destinations. Bowling center operators considering expansion or repositioning will find the case studies instructive.

articles.title: IATP Partners with TheHopeLine to Support Mental Health of Young Employees and Guests
articles.summary: The International Adventure and Trampoline Parks Association has partnered with TheHopeLine, a free 24/7 crisis chat service, to connect young employees and guests with mental health support resources. IATP will introduce the service to its member operators as part of its broader commitment to staff and guest wellbeing. For trampoline park and FEC operators with large youth workforces, this partnership offers a low-cost, high-impact resource to add to their HR toolkit.

articles.title: TrainerTainment to Present Staff Training Session at Amusement 360 Conference
articles.summary: TrainerTainment's Genevieve Sullivan will speak at Amusement 360 on designing staff training programs that produce lasting behavioral change rather than short-term compliance. The session, titled 'Build it Once: Designing Staff Training That Sticks,' targets FEC operators frustrated with training retention issues. Given persistent labor challenges in the industry, actionable training strategies remain a top operational priority.

articles.title: Semnox and Uplay Complete Six Venue Management System Deployments Across Benelux
articles.summary: Semnox and its regional partner Uplay have successfully completed venue management system installations across six FEC locations in Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg over the past year. The deployments cover cashless payment, access control, and operational reporting infrastructure. The companies will be showcasing their integrated platform at IAAPA Expo Europe 2026 in London, making it a key stop for operators evaluating management technology.

articles.title: Fun Spot America Launches Early-Access 2027 Season Pass Sale with Free 2026 Admission
articles.summary: Fun Spot America is running its first-ever Early Access Season Pass promotion, offering discounted 2027 season passes that include free admission for the remainder of 2026 — up to 16 months of access. The promotion is designed to lock in recurring revenue ahead of the next season while rewarding early buyers. FEC operators looking for creative membership and pass retention strategies will find this campaign worth examining.

articles.title: Bergen County FEC Equipment Auction Includes Trampolines, Bowling Lanes, and VR Arena
articles.summary: A large family entertainment center in Bergen County, New Jersey is liquidating its assets via auction, with inventory including trampolines, bowling lanes, and a virtual reality arena. For operators planning new venues or expanding existing ones, the auction presents a potential opportunity to acquire quality used equipment at below-market prices. The closure also signals continued consolidation pressure on mid-market multi-attraction FEC venues.

articles.title: Guy Fieri's Downtown Flavortown FEC Opens at Myrtle Beach Mall
articles.summary: Celebrity chef Guy Fieri and FACE Amusement Group are hosting the official ribbon cutting for Downtown Flavortown Myrtle Beach on September 10, 2026, at Myrtle Beach Mall. The venue blends food and entertainment in a celebrity-branded FEC format, part of a growing trend of IP- and personality-driven entertainment destinations. Operators and investors should watch this concept's early performance as a signal for the viability of celebrity-branded FEC partnerships.

articles.title: Six Flags Expands Halloween Portfolio with 29 Licensed Haunted Attractions Across Its Parks
articles.summary: Six Flags is scaling up its 2026 Halloween season with 29 new and returning licensed haunted attractions, 196 themed scare zones, and expanded nighttime ride experiences across its portfolio. The heavy IP licensing approach signals a broader industry trend toward branded seasonal events as key revenue drivers. Independent FEC operators running Halloween events can draw lessons from Six Flags' multi-layered programming strategy.

articles.title: XBOX and BBC Studios to Share LBE and IP Licensing Insights at Brand Licensing Europe 2026
articles.summary: XBOX and BBC Studios will lead sessions at Brand Licensing Europe 2026 in October, specifically addressing the fast-growing location-based experiences market and lessons learned in franchise licensing. For FEC operators exploring IP partnerships, hearing directly from major licensors about what makes LBE deals work is a significant opportunity. The conference takes place October 6-8 at ExCel London.

articles.title: Two New Bowling Alleys Set to Open in Western Australia
articles.summary: Two new bowling venues are slated to open in Western Australia, adding to the growing supply of bowling-anchored entertainment options in the region. The openings reflect continued investment in bowling as a core FEC attraction in markets outside North America. Suppliers and operators tracking global bowling industry growth will want to follow these developments.

articles.title: Jersey Shore Former Drugstore to Be Converted into Family Entertainment Center
articles.summary: A long-vacant drugstore on the Jersey Shore is being repurposed into a family entertainment center, continuing the trend of adaptive retail reuse for FEC development. Construction is underway at the former Ship Bottom CVS site, with Fantasy Island Entertainment Center taking over the space. The project is a textbook example of how FEC operators are capitalizing on the availability of vacant retail real estate in high-traffic tourist corridors.

articles.title: AromaPrime to Unveil Pirate Water Ride Scent at IAAPA Expo Europe
articles.summary: AromaPrime will debut its new Pirate Water Ride themed scent oil at IAAPA Expo Europe in London this September, targeting both theme parks and attraction retail. Scent theming is an increasingly recognized tool for enhancing immersive guest experiences across FEC environments. Operators attending IAAPA Expo Europe should add this to their product discovery list.

articles.title: Calypso's Cove Adds Real JCB Mini Excavator Ride Attraction
articles.summary: Calypso's Cove in Old Forge, New York has added an Excavator attraction featuring real JCB mini excavators sourced from its sister park, Diggerland USA. The hands-on, operator-controlled ride format appeals to young children and families seeking interactive experiences beyond passive amusement rides. The addition is a practical example of cross-venue asset sharing to add differentiated attractions without major capital outlay.

articles.title: Dollywood Opens NightFlight Expedition, Its Largest Single Attraction Investment Ever
articles.summary: Dollywood has opened NightFlight Expedition, a new indoor adventure roller coaster that represents the largest single attraction investment in the park's history and its 11th coaster. While Dollywood operates at a larger scale than most FECs, the investment underscores the industry-wide emphasis on signature anchor attractions to drive visitation and media attention. The indoor format and theming approach offer design inspiration for FEC operators planning major attraction additions.

articles.title: Disney Patents Personalized Ride Recommendation System Based on Guest Preferences and Aversions
articles.summary: Disney has been granted a patent for a system that matches guests with attractions based on their stated preferences, dislikes, and health conditions, going well beyond the basic recommendations currently in its park apps. The technology stores individual user profiles and compares them against real-time attraction data to surface personalized suggestions. As guest experience personalization becomes a competitive differentiator, FEC operators and technology vendors should monitor how this approach evolves and consider analogous applications for their own booking and kiosk systems.

articles.title: Adventure Landing Closes Raleigh Location After 38 Years of Operation
articles.summary: Adventure Landing's Raleigh venue has permanently closed after nearly four decades, ending a long run for one of the region's most recognizable multi-attraction FEC brands. The closure follows a period of increased competition from newer, more experiential entertainment venues in the market. The story serves as a cautionary tale for legacy FEC operators who have not kept pace with evolving consumer expectations.

articles.title: Urban Story Ventures Announces $350M 'The Bend' Entertainment Project in Chattanooga
articles.summary: Urban Story Ventures has announced a $350 million mixed-use entertainment development called The Bend in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Projects of this scale increasingly anchor large-format entertainment and hospitality destinations that draw visitors from across a region. FEC operators, investors, and suppliers tracking large-scale domestic entertainment development pipelines should follow this project's progress.

articles.title: Tornado Terry's Family Amusement Center Turns to GoFundMe in Bid to Stay Open
articles.summary: Tornado Terry's Family Amusement Center in the Keller-Roanoke area of North Texas has launched a GoFundMe campaign in what the owner describes as a last-ditch effort to keep the business open. The situation highlights the financial fragility facing small, independent amusement center operators in competitive suburban markets. Industry stakeholders should be aware of the growing number of legacy small FECs struggling to survive without a modernization strategy or financial lifeline.
